Working from: `Brief` of idea-repo (revision 2), objective `story-repo#1`. This page says **what to test and what each part of the paper says**; it never says what a result must be. Where a result decides between two stories, both are written below (§6) so nobody has to rewrite the paper's frame after the fact.

## Venue frame (venue-repo, `story-repo`#4)
NeurIPS 2026 Main Track; **9 content pages including figures and tables**; references, appendix and checklist outside. **Contribution type: General** (an evaluation paper: controlled comparison, bias–variance accounting, ceiling analysis), also if the headline turns out conditional or negative: "Negative Results" is not chosen (high significance/originality bar). **Main body: 7 items** — Fig. 1, Table 2, Fig. 2, Fig. 3, Fig. 4, Fig. 5, Fig. 6 (Fig. 1 is a small schematic). Everything else is appendix: Table 1 (audit and split/target counts), Table 3, Table 4, Fig. 5b, per-benchmark tables. Evidence a claim rests on is in the main body: the main text carries the k targets / #families per split in Table 2's columns and one sentence on thin cells, and says where Table 1 is. Writing profile: abstract one paragraph ≈ 130–260 words stating claims, scope and the headline; introduction ≈ 550–1500 words with the result stated; first figure on page 1–2; short related work in the main text, long version in the appendix; the checklist's "Claims" item is checked against the evidence.

## 0. The paper in one paragraph
Evaluating an LLM on a full benchmark is costly, so we run it on n ≪ N items and predict its full score. Existing methods (anchor points, tinyBenchmarks, metabench, assessor, active acquisition) use the score matrix of *source models* to pick items and fit a *latent model* of the target; they are judged mostly on held-out models that resemble the sources. We cast the problem as **finite-population estimation of a mean of N unknown 0/1 values with a free covariate (the source matrix)**. That frame separates what the sources can buy — **variance reduction** — from what must be controlled by design — **bias**. We (i) test, on 13 binary matrices and under three target splits (interpolation, extrapolation, lineage-held-out), whether model-based predictors lose accuracy where targets differ from the sources; (ii) test whether a design-based correction (probability sampling with a positivity floor + difference/GREG estimator) repairs it and at what variance cost; (iii) measure how much the source matrix can help at all over plain stratified/balanced random sampling; (iv) examine ordering of models separately from score error. A negative or conditional answer to any of these is a result.

Working title (not final): *What do source models buy? Design-based benchmark prediction from a few items.*

Primary endpoint (fixed before running): **RMSE ratio to uniform random sampling at n = 100 items, geometric mean over benchmarks, paired clustered bootstrap CI, per split.** One **secondary** endpoint at fixed n/N = 2% (n = 100 is ~18% of IFEval, N≈541, but <1% of MMLU-Pro, N≈12k, so the geometric mean mixes very different n/N). Conclusions must hold at both n=100 and n/N=2%, or are reported as scale-dependent. Neither is changed after seeing curves. Everything else is secondary.

# Protocol (fixed before any method was scored on targets)

Written 2026-11-26 before running `scripts/02_run.py`. Changes after seeing results are logged in the section "Deviations" at the end, with the reason.

## Data
13 binary matrices (7 Open LLM Leaderboard v2, 6 HELM) of `data.md`, commit 55faff49…; see `scripts/00_download.sh`, audit in `results/audit.csv`.
Pre-processing (`src/bpred/data.py`): OLL models repeated under the same name are dropped (keep first); any model whose response vector is identical to an earlier model's is dropped (keep first); items answered identically by all models are kept (they contribute zero variance and make the problem easier for no method in particular; counted in the audit). HELM row→model names come from `helm_model_list.txt` (83 rows); `legalbench` has 79 rows with no published row→name mapping, so its families are unknown (each row its own family; it is excluded from the lineage split and its extrapolation/interpolation CIs cluster by row).
Family = first matching keyword of the lower-cased model name (`family_of`, e.g. qwen, llama, mistral, openai-gpt, claude), else the organisation prefix. Heuristic; checked on the audit output.

## Splits (per benchmark; sources = models given to the method, targets = models only scored at the end)
- **interp** — random 5-fold over models (seed 0); targets = the fold, sources = the other 4 folds. Near-duplicates (same family) stay in the sources.
- **lineage** — 5-fold over *families* (families assigned to folds by greedy size balancing, seed 0); targets = the families of the fold, sources = every other family. Not run for legalbench.
- **extrap** — targets = the top 25 % of models by full-benchmark score, sources = the rest; hence every target is above every source (ties at the boundary resolved by dropping tied targets). One configuration per benchmark; subset draws are the only replication.
Thin cells: a (benchmark, split) with fewer than 10 targets or fewer than 5 independent families among targets is flagged "thin", excluded from the main aggregate and shown with them included as well.

## Budget and the primary endpoint
n grid {10, 25, 50, 100, 200, 400} restricted to n ≤ N/2 (so some small benchmarks have fewer points). **Primary n = 100** (reported with n/N). **Primary endpoint:** RMSE ratio to uniform random sampling at n = 100, where RMSE = sqrt(mean over targets and subset draws of (pred − true full score)²) per (benchmark, split) and ratio = RMSE_method / RMSE_uniform on the same draws and targets; aggregated by geometric mean over benchmarks (non-thin; plus all). CIs: bootstrap over families (resampling target families, with all draws of a family kept) — "paired" because the ratio is formed inside each bootstrap replicate. Everything else (MAE, signed bias, Spearman, Kendall, top-decile precision, pairwise order accuracy vs true gap δ, error vs true score) is secondary. Rank correlations: per (fold, draw) over targets, then averaged over folds and draws.
Draws: R = 10 independent subsets per (fold, n) for interp and lineage, R = 40 for extrap (single fold). One subset per draw serves all targets. Deterministic designs (info-top-n; CAT, which depends on the target only) have no draw variance; they count once.

## Methods (all selection/tuning uses sources only; target contributes its n answers; same n for every method; shared seeds)
Designs: `uniform`, `strat` (sorted-by-source-difficulty systematic: one random item per stratum of N/n items), `pps` (π_i = n[(1−ε)w_i/Σw + ε/N], w_i = √(p̂_i(1−p̂_i)), systematic PPS in difficulty order, π capped at 1), `balanced` (greedy forward selection from a random pool of 4n items so that the subset mean reproduces every source's full score), `anchor` (k-means with n clusters on the item×source response matrix, medoid per cluster, weight = cluster size), `infotop` (top-n items by 2PL Fisher information averaged over source abilities), `cat` (adaptive max-information 2PL, per target).

cat > /tmp/req.md <<'EOF'
Request (idea → analysis): run one more estimator family, and check one possible artefact, because results-v1 leave the extrapolation question half-answered.

**Why.** In results-v1 (ccb6895), in extrapolation the source-tuned-λ difference estimator is shrunk (inner "targets" are not above the real ones), fixed λ=1 removes the bias but buys little over stratified sampling, and pure model-based predictors lose by bias. The Brief (rev 3, §3b) adds the one estimator that does not need the target to resemble the sources or any source-side tuning that mimics the outer split.

**1. Target-recalibrated regression estimator (Brief §3b), any design (uniform, strat, pps, balanced):**
- fit on the target's n answers, weighted LS with weights 1/π: y_i ~ β0 + β1·s_i (+ β2·p̂_i^{CF});
- s_i = logit of the source mean accuracy of item i (source-only); optional second feature p̂_i^{CF} = cross-fitted IRT prediction (5-fold over the sample, as for `diff-irt`); ridge-stabilised if needed at n=10–25, said in the notes;
- estimate = mean of the fitted values over all N items (equivalently ȳ_Hájek + (x̄_all − x̄_S)'β̂); predictions clipped to [0,1];
- no hyperparameter tuned on sources except what is already fixed (feature set chosen on the source-only inner split, and a single choice for all splits stated in advance).
- Report in the same tables as the other estimators: ratio to uniform and to strat at n=100 and n/N=2%, all five splits, signed bias per target, per-target bias/variance, so it enters the primary-endpoint family as a method class ("target-recalibrated"), with the "post-hoc best of a grid" caveat the outline already sets. Priority: extrap, extrap10, extrap50, then interp, lineage.

**2. A possible artefact in `irt-model`/`irt-plugin` in extrapolation (RMSE ≈ 1.5–2× uniform):** is the MAP ability estimate shrunk by its prior toward the source mean (and items no source solves have clamped difficulty)? A check: the same predictor with a flat/weak prior (ML ability, or prior variance ×10) on extrap, to say whether "model-based predictors are biased above the sources" is a property of model-based prediction or of that prior. If it is the prior, the paper should say so; a model-based baseline that ignores it is a weak comparator.

**3. Optional, lower priority (Brief §3c):** two-phase target-adaptive design (n/2 stratified, then n/2 with π ∝ √(p̂(θ̂)(1−p̂(θ̂))) plus floor, conditional π in the estimator) on the extrap splits only, paired with strat and pps at the same n. Skip if cost is a problem; say "not run".

What this serves: Brief C2 (does a bias-by-design correction repair extrapolation, at what cost) and C3 (what the sources can buy). Whatever the outcome, it is reported; if the recalibrated estimator is no better than `balanced|diffnaive-irt`, that is also a finding.
EOF

shown.message:
I kept the Brief's two contributions as they were, and added a stronger extrapolation method to the plan (Brief rev 3). I answered and closed `story-repo`'s request (`idea-repo`#4). No new experiments have run since results-v1.

- **Contributions C2 and C3:** the results-v1 findings `story-repo` listed are acceptable outcomes of those tests.
  - The difference-corrected estimators help most in interpolation and lineage splits.
  - In extrapolation they give a modest gain over stratified sampling and remove the bias.
  - The source-tuned weight fails because tuning inside the sources can't reproduce targets above all sources.
  - I told `story-repo` to state the extrapolation value as robustness, not a large accuracy win.
- **Why I changed the idea:** in extrapolation, results-v1 is only half-answered. The best methods beat stratified sampling by about 10% or less. Brief rev 3 adds one estimator that needs no tuning on source models. Its slope is fitted on the target's own n answers: the sources say which items are harder, and the target's sample says how hard they are for it. It also adds an optional two-phase design that re-weights the second half of the sample using the target's own ability estimate.
- **Request to analysis:** I opened `experiment-repo`#6 asking them to run both. The first is the priority; it should be reported in the same tables as the other estimators. I also asked them to check whether the model-based predictors' extrapolation failure comes partly from the ability prior shrinking the target's estimate toward the source mean. If it does, those predictors were a weak comparator.
- **Hold on the extrapolation headline:** I asked `story-repo` to hold the extrapolation headline wording until `experiment-repo`#6 comes back. The estimator was added after seeing results-v1, so the paper has to say that. Interpolation, lineage and ceiling statements are unaffected.
